title: THE BLACK BOULÉ & BOURGEOISIE IN THE BIBLE

sense.text:
This was spoken when we were making our exodus out of Egypt, on the continent of Africa, on our way to the land of Canaan, the land of Ham. Neither Egypt nor Canaan was in Europe.

“If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”: right there the verse shows what the true religion is. People ask what the true religion is, and God answers it: his commandments. Nothing else. You can’t add to that and you can’t take away from that. His religion is his commandments, and “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee” when we would not keep them.

“Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people”: another race. The people of Kenya were given to the British, Ghana was given to the British, and we were given to America.

It is still happening in 2025. Slave trade is going on in Libya. After Muammar Gaddafi was killed by rebels with the help of NATO, Libya became a slave market where Africans are sold for as little as $300. Naima Jamal, a sister from Ethiopia, is being sold there, bound and gagged, and the men behind her are not even tied up, because their spirits are broken. That is the Arabs taking us. You could never do this to the Chinese, the white man, East Indians or Arabs; their nations would rain hell on your head. But it is done to black people, with 54 countries in Africa and not one stopping it. Ethiopia has a military and does nothing, because they don’t give a damn about their own people. And the Arabs over there are Muslim, and the black Muslims are silent about it and make believe they see nothing.

This should infuriate you. You always have to put your race first. White people put white people first and Arabs put Arabs first, but when black people put black people first, they call it racist. So I won’t shed one tear for those Arabs as long as this goes on. The Lord has to give us power, and when he does, we’ll end this overnight, and those Arabs will never lift a hand against our people again.

“And there shall be no might in thine hand”: no military might, no economic might, no political might. What we just witnessed is the evidence. Many think these curses have come and gone, but they are still in effect today.

“The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway.” This is the proof, the evidence, that the Bible is a true book. Don’t tell me the Bible isn’t real when I’m reading things I see taking place this year.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”: “in hunger, and in thirst”, that is food and water, “and in nakedness”, clothing, “and in want of all things”: education, religion, medicine. For all of it we have to go to our enemies. “And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.”

How can you read that and say it never happened? That is what the Trump administration is trying to do in getting rid of critical race theory and changing the museums, saying the Smithsonian has too much slave history in it. It is a direct attack against the Bible. People don’t see the connection because the Bible has always been taught as a fairy tale book, but certain white people understand that through the Israelites the Bible is a history and prophetic book. So they say, get the history out of the schools, and that way the Bible is made of no effect. That is the plan. But they shall fail.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”: when we went under the Arab slave trade we mingled among them and were forced to worship their god, the fake god Allah, the black Kaaba stone; that is serving “other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We intermarried among the Arabs and the Nilotic people too. That is why some of our people have that Arabic look, and some have that dark, deep Nilotic look, from mixing and intermingling. Some of us were taken throughout the Americas and England and mixed in there, and some have that high yellow look. We have always been different complexions.

Egypt, from the Hebrew name Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships” is tribulation; in other words, slavery, and it came “with ships.”

“Thou shalt see it no more again”: in captivity we would not see ancient Egypt again. “And there ye shall be sold unto your enemies”: wherever those ships took us, we were sold to our enemies, “for bondmen and bondwomen”, slave men and slave women. “And no man shall buy you” means no man shall redeem us.

The Christian apologists say the Israelites were never sold as slaves, and they try to pervert this verse with the NIV to say you would try to sell yourselves but no one would buy you. That’s BS. The scriptures show we were bought and sold.

precepts.why:
“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.” Pure religion is what God commanded; this verse is making reference to his laws.

When it speaks of visiting the fatherless and widows, it goes right back to the law: Deuteronomy 14:29 and Exodus 22:22. So all of it goes back to God’s law. That is what religion is: God’s law, the commandments of Deuteronomy 28:15.

The law that pure religion points back to: “the Levite, (because he hath no part nor inheritance with thee,) and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, which are within thy gates, shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied; that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hand which thou doest.” We had to take care of the Levite, the fatherless and the widow, so that the Lord might bless us. That is the religion, and it is a commandment.

“Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child.” Another of the laws behind James 1:27. Visiting the fatherless and widows is not something new; it is God’s law, and that is what the true religion is.

“Mine heritage is unto me as a speckled bird.” A speckled bird is different colors. Among the twelve tribes we have always had different complexions.

So nobody has to think he is being told he is mixed with the white man. Some of us are and some of us aren’t, but God’s heritage has always been of many complexions, and the scattering of Deuteronomy 28:64 added to it.

For the dumb, stupid Christian apologists who say the Israelites were never sold as slaves: “And the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves.” Write that down. The children of Israel were bought for slaves, as Deuteronomy 28:68 said they would be sold unto their enemies.

“And there were destroyed within the space of three whole days fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.” We were being sold left and right by the Greeks, and the Greeks are the white man.

This is for the stupid Edomite apologist who makes us his business, Mark Riser, whose wife left him for a black man, and all who say Israel was never sold. Forty thousand slain and no fewer sold.

“And I will set my face against you”: God set his face against our people. “And ye shall be slain before your enemies”: we were slain before our enemies. “They that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you.”

That is what being sold unto our enemies in Deuteronomy 28:68 brought: those who hate us rule over us.

sense.text: Here we jump up in history. “Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it.” First identify mount Seir: Genesis 36:8 says Esau dwelt there, and Esau is Edom. So God is commanding Ezekiel, and he is commanding us, to prophesy against Esau, Edom.

“Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity.” Perpetual hatred means everlasting. Their hatred is not going to stop against us.

“In the time that their iniquity had an end”: our iniquity allegedly had an end in 1865, when we were allegedly emancipated. But it didn’t end there.

precepts.why: “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” This identifies mount Seir. Esau and the Edomites lived in mount Seir, so when Ezekiel is told to set his face against mount Seir and prophesy against it, God is commanding us to prophesy against Esau, Edom.

This shows what happened after the alleged end in 1865. “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease”: the heathen are the other nations. “For I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.”

They helped forward the affliction. They set up the Ku Klux Klan, the Black Codes, redlining, all manner of things. In 1865 and early 1866 the all-white governments in the South set up under Andrew Johnson passed the Black Codes to get the plantation system going again: not as slave labor but as forced labor. Black people had no right to vote, sit on juries, or testify in court against white people; they had to sign year-long labor contracts with a white employer or be called vagrants, arrested and fined, and if they couldn’t pay they were auctioned off to a white man who would pay the fine. A black man working for himself on his own land was illegal, and Mississippi barred black people from even owning land so that they had no choice but to work for white planters.

God speaks to these Black Codes and to slavery: “Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed.” A decree is a mandate, a law. Imagine owning land and being arrested as a vagrant because you work for yourself. That is some evil stuff.

They prescribed it “To turn aside the needy from judgment”, to turn us aside from true judgment, as we just witnessed, “and to take away the right from the poor of my people.” Not all people: my people, God says. “That widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless!”

This is what happened from Assyria all the way up to the United States of America. After the Black Codes came Jim Crow.

sense.text:
“And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations.” A proverb is a joke. We have become a joke among the nations.

Look at the Jim Crow images and how they drew us: giant pink lips, the picaninny babies, the joke that you babysit black babies by wetting their lips and sticking them to a wall, the minstrel shows, Aunt Jemima on the pancake box, the hungry colored boy going for roast chicken, the black woman beating her husband in Sugarfoot Jones. Amos and Andy were humiliating, but that was the only work they gave us. Mr. Popo in Dragon Ball Z, the fat black servant beside Goku, is a mockery of black people; these cartoons give black people low self-esteem, and some of you grew up on them and look just like that.

Today it is the AI cartoons mocking black people, especially black women, all over, and nobody calls that racist. But when they hear us talk, they say that’s racist.

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.” We are a scorn and a derision to those round about us. “Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.” This is a curse upon us: a byword, a proverb, a joke, the way they mock us.

These images are the examples of what God prophesied would happen if we broke the commandments. We didn’t believe him, so now we live it.

Jim Crow was not a person but a minstrel character played by a white man in blackface, and his name became the shorthand for a system of laws built to keep black people at the bottom for almost a hundred years: poll taxes and impossible literacy tests to strip us of the vote, segregation everywhere down to the cemeteries, prisons turned into plantations through arrests for vagrancy and leasing to the coal mines and cotton fields, redlining that kept black families from buying property and building generational wealth, lynching, rape and burning with impunity, and the psychological warfare of calling white men sir and stepping off the sidewalk. It was slavery under a different name.

sense.text:
This shows what occurred from Jim Crow all the way up till now. “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets”: our young men hang on the corners. “As a wild bull in a net”: these young men are like wild bulls, and the net is the system.

“They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God”: all the curses in Deuteronomy 28 are falling upon our people, and young black men don’t understand why.
“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine.” We are not drunk with wine. We are drunk with religion, drunk with politics, drunk with lies.

“Thus saith thy Lord the Lord, and thy God that pleadeth the cause of his people.” We want America or Africa or some country to plead our cause, but no country ever stands up for us. God is the only one who will plead for us. If you are waiting for Africa to stand up for you, hold your breath; you’ll drop dead.

“Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again.”

“But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee”: the curses that came upon us, God will put on those that afflict us.

Those that afflicted us said to our soul, “Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over.” That is Jim Crow. We let white people walk all over us. They did it back then and you see it even today, especially among black Christians. At that memorial for Kirk, the white speakers said white people are the real Christians and that Donald Trump is their sword against evil men in this country, and not one black Christian, not one urban apologist, said a word.

Think of what was done to Judah to keep him down, the laws passed so he could not own land. The little freedom we have here is because Judah went through it. So those who come here running their mouths calling Judah lazy don’t know history; their minds are colonized and they talk like the white man.

When we started doing well back in the 1920s, in places like Rosewood, they bombed us, dropped dynamite on us, and stole the homes and lands we had. The signs said Jim Crow must go, and America is our jail as long as Jim Crow lives. Guess what: America is still your jail.

Many of the HBCUs, the colleges the black fraternities and sororities come from, require you to take an oath. The Boulé, Sigma Pi Phi, founded in 1904, was a secret society of black elites that wanted to be on par with Skull and Bones, and it is the father of the Divine Nine fraternities and sororities. These schools were not built by black people either; white philanthropists like Carnegie and Rockefeller channelled millions into them. You oath takers in these schools, and you who send your kids there, are taking demonic oaths to Satan.

“Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths”: if you make an oath, you perform your oath to the Lord.

“But I say unto you”: watch what Christ says. “Swear not at all”: don’t take an oath at all. “Neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King”, the city of King David.

“Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.” Don’t even swear by the hair of your head, because you can’t turn your hair black or white on your own just by a thought. Hair dye has nothing to do with it.

“But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay”: yes, yes and no, no. “For whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.” That is why Christ said make no oaths, don’t swear, make no vows. They are all alike, and he said don’t do it.

precepts.why:
Nobody should think that if you were part of this stuff you can’t repent. You can repent of all sins. “All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men.”

The blasphemy against the Holy Ghost is when you reject Christ and reject his truth. Some of you were in the fraternities and sororities, and thank God you came out; that sin can be forgiven.

We are still dealing with the oath takers who go to the HBCUs and the fraternities and sororities. “When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it”: you’d better pay it, “for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.”

“Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.” This is what Christ was saying: don’t vow, don’t make an oath. “Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin”, because judgment will come on you; “neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?”

sense.text:
“Thou shalt have no other gods before me.” Depending on the fraternity or sorority, they have symbols that represent their house, and when you make these oaths there are often gods that come with it. You are involved with false gods.

All the Divine Nine are tied to them: Anubis, the dog-headed god of the dead, to the Q dogs; Thoth, the god of the moon and magic, to the Kappas; Athena, also called Minerva, the goddess of wisdom, war and craft, to the Deltas, whose hand sign is the eye of Lucifer; Atlas the Titan to the AKAs. If you are in one, you are in a cult.

precepts.why:
“And against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am the Lord.” He passed through the land of Egypt that night and smote all the firstborn, both man and beast.

God has always been against all these false gods. When you join these fraternities, you have given your allegiance to false gods, the very gods of Egypt God executed judgment against.

The whole fourteenth chapter goes into idolatry, and verses 22 and 23 give the key points. “Moreover this was not enough for them, that they erred in the knowledge of God”: when you are in idolatry you have erred from the knowledge of God, because God said thou shalt have no other gods before him, thou shalt not take his name in vain, and no idols or images to bow down to.

“But whereas they lived in the great war of ignorance, those so great plagues called they peace.” Dealing in idolatry, you are in a great war of ignorance, and you think you are living in peace. People are at peace when they live in ignorance.

“For whilst they slew their children in sacrifices”: abortions. Black women have murdered over 19 million babies since 1973, more homicides than the Ku Klux Klan committed. They say a baby isn’t a baby until it is born, yet when a pregnant black woman is killed it is called a double homicide. Nobody sees the wordplay, the trickery that Esau does.

“Or used secret ceremonies”: black people wanted to be on par with white people, to equal Skull and Bones, so the HBCUs created those fraternities, secret organizations that picked out the smartest and the brightest. “Or made revellings of strange rites”: hazing. Caleb Wilson, a twenty-year-old at Southern University, died after collapsing during a fraternity ritual. These are not team-building exercises; they are spiritual covenants.

sense.text:
The Omega Psi Phi oath swears to uphold the fraternity under the penalty of having the right hand lose her cunning and the tongue cleave to the roof of the mouth. They took the Bible and put it in that crack. That is evil black people stuff.

“If I forget thee, O Jerusalem”: if I forget my homeland. When you forget your homeland, you forget your identity. “Let my right hand forget her cunning”: I will not be able to be successful in this world in raising up Jerusalem.

“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth”: meaning you cannot teach the Bible correctly. “If I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy.”

The negro took that and put it in one of those stupid fraternity oaths. God is going to give a judgment for that.

precepts.why:
“If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city.” There is a judgment for that. Taking these oaths that take parts of the Bible and pervert them brings judgment.

So if you stay in those fraternities and don’t renounce it, there is a judgment. When we repent of our sins we have to repent of everything. You can’t repent of adultery and not repent of the oath you made to your fraternity. Repent of all of it and confess it to the Lord.

sense.text:
The fraternities and sororities take the names: Alpha Phi Alpha, Alpha Tau Omega, Alpha Epsilon Pi, Omega Psi Phi, Alpha Kappa Alpha, Alpha Gamma Delta, Alpha Sigma Alpha. But Christ says, “I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last.” The only Alpha and Omega is Jesus Christ, the black Messiah, not your fraternity. If you don’t repent, you are blaspheming and going against Almighty God.

“What thou seest, write in a book”: Christ commands John to write down what he sees in a book, what we call the Bible today, “and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia.”
“I saw seven golden candlesticks”: that is the menorah.
“And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man, clothed with a garment down to the foot, and girt about the paps with a golden girdle.”

“His head and his hairs were white like wool”: the hair on his head and the hair on his face were white like wool. Wool is a texture; afro hair, we call it. “And his eyes were as a flame of fire”, because Christ drank wine in moderation.

“And his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace.” When you burn brass in a furnace, see how black it gets. It is describing Jesus Christ as a black man: not a Caucasian, not a European, not a Frenchman, but a black man. That is the Holy Bible’s description of Christ.

This is one of the origins of these black fraternities. After the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus Epiphanes took the kingdom, “Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest.” The high priesthood was up for bid. In the law you had to come through Aaron’s line to be high priest, but when the Greeks took over, they bid for it with money.

He promised the king hundreds of talents of silver, and more besides, “if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.” Not only did he want to buy the high priesthood; he promised to bring the Israelites into the Greek way of training and call them Antiochians.
“He forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.” Jason, the brother of Onias, brought Israel to the Greek fashion.

He took away the privileges granted the Jews, “and putting down the governments which were according to the law, he brought up new customs against the law.” He built “a place of exercise under the tower itself, and brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat.”

“Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest.” This is the history Christians don’t know about and don’t understand.

“The priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth.”

“Not setting by the honours of their fathers”: the Israelites did not set by the honours of their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.” We liked the glory of the Greeks best of all. Hence your fraternities: they like the glory of the Greeks best of all.

“For they had them to be their enemies and avengers.” At one time the Greeks were our enemies; then they became our avengers: help us and avenge us, O Greeks. “Whose custom they followed so earnestly, and unto whom they desired to be like in all things.” Our people desired to be like the Greeks in all things, and it is still going on today.

precepts.why:
“Neither was it lawful for a man to keep sabbath days or ancient feasts, or to profess himself at all to be a Jew.” Don’t be surprised if these laws come back. That law was just passed in France; that is why they dissolved the IUIC school in France. They said it is unlawful to keep sabbath days and the ancient feasts or to say you are a Jew; to say you are a Jew in France is anti-Semitic, hate speech. Some think it will never happen in America. Don’t be surprised.

“And in the day of the king’s birth every month they were brought by bitter constraint to eat of the sacrifices.” We never celebrated birthdays; they forced us to celebrate theirs. “And when the feast of Bacchus was kept, the Jews were compelled to go in procession to Bacchus, carrying ivy.” The Bacchus procession today is the Labor Day West Indian Day parade in Brooklyn: it is all bacchanal. Now nobody has to force them; thousands of West Indians come from everywhere to keep the holiday we were once forced to keep.

“Moreover there went out a decree”, laws made against the Jews, “that they should observe the same fashions”: we had to observe the same fashions as the Greeks, “and whoso would not conform themselves to the manners of the Gentiles should be put to death.” That was the law then, and that is how we became Gentiles in the New Testament. Our people desiring to be like the Greeks in all things began under force; today they do it willingly.

sense.text:
The Divine Nine, the black sororities and fraternities that have always been a political force and took center stage in the 2024 election, are like groups in the Bible, such as the Herodians. The Herodians were a political group of Jews, black people, who supported the Herodian dynasty and sought to keep Herod’s rule in Judea under Roman authority. The Pharisees were religious and the Herodians were political, and though they were opposed to each other, the two joined together to destroy Christ. Christ warned of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod. The Herodians were compromisers who believed a client kingdom under the Herods was the best option, and they chose Herod over Christ.

“Simeon that was called Niger”: Niger means black. They were called black.

“And Manaen, which had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.” Saul is the one who later became Paul. They went to the same schools of learning.

“And they send unto him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.” The Pharisees were religious and the Herodians were political, and the Herodians supported the Edomite named Herod. Together they wanted to catch Christ in his words.

precepts.why:
“Then went the Pharisees, and took counsel how they might entangle him in his talk. And they sent out unto him their disciples with the Herodians.” They asked, “Is it lawful to give tribute unto Cesar, or not?” Is it lawful to pay taxes?

“But Jesus perceived their wickedness”, called for the tribute money, and asked, “Whose is this image and superscription?” “Render therefore unto Cesar the things which are Cesar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.” They couldn’t catch Christ in his words about taxes, because he paid taxes. They knew that by not paying taxes, Rome could arrest you and execute you.

You have that going on today. People in the congregation in Oklahoma City said they were sovereign and didn’t have to pay taxes, and they lost their houses, their jobs, everything; without a social security card, a driver’s license or an identity, they get fired, and then they are upset with us. If you are getting rid of your birth certificate, social security, driver’s license and citizenship, you are an idiot. When they put you out of the country, what country can you go to with no passport?

Another group, blacks and Latinos, said no idols and no images, took a black marker to the dollar bill and blacked out the pyramid, the eye, the eagle, United States and George Washington’s face, then went to the store to pay with it and were thrown out. Some Israelites learn a little knowledge and exit stage left into stupidity.
“And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.” The political group and the religious group both wanted to destroy Christ.

sense.text: Here is the bourgeoisie, the black bourgeoisie, in the scriptures. “And there was a great cry of the people and of their wives against their brethren the Jews.” They said they had to take up corn for these certain Jews that they might eat and live.
“We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses, that we might buy corn, because of the dearth.” “We have borrowed money for the king’s tribute”: we borrowed money to pay taxes.

“Lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them.” Our sons and daughters are working for these other Jews, black Jews, and we can’t even redeem them, because we’re broke, “for other men have our lands and vineyards.”

Nehemiah was very angry, “and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers.” The nobles were a group of intellectuals who were very wealthy. These are your bourgeois. “Ye exact usury, every one of his brother.” Usury means interest, extreme interest, like twenty percent.

“We after our ability have redeemed our brethren the Jews, which were sold unto the heathen; and will ye even sell your brethren?” See what we started to do to ourselves. We were redeemed from the Persians and Medes, we got back into our own land, and now we were putting each other in captivity. “Then held they their peace, and found nothing to answer.”

“It is not good that ye do.” “I pray you, let us leave off this usury”: leave off the interest you put on the people. “Restore, I pray you, to them, even this day, their lands, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, also the hundredth part of the money”, the interest they took.

“We will restore them, and will require nothing of them.” “Then I called the priests, and took an oath of them.” Nehemiah got all Israel against the nobles. Sometimes a show of force is necessary to get these rich black people off your back, because at times they will do worse to you than the white man. That is what was going on in Nehemiah 5.

“Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite”: these two were of other nations. “It grieved them exceedingly that there was come a man to seek the welfare of the children of Israel.”

The other nations always get angry when somebody looks out for the welfare of black people. That’s why they killed Martin Luther King: he was looking out for the welfare of black people. Yet they always have his name in their mouths, asking what Martin Luther King would say, manipulating his speeches to get us to perform. We wouldn’t know, would we? You killed him.
Sanballat and Tobiah were of other nations, not Israelites, and now there is “Geshem the Arabian”, an Arab. “And the rest of our enemies”: notice what it calls them. Our enemies.
“Come, let us meet together in some one of the villages in the plain of Ono. But they thought to do me mischief.” They wanted to kill him.

“I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease, whilst I leave it, and come down to you?” Nehemiah’s attitude is our attitude: we are doing a great work, and we don’t have time for you.

It’s the same today. There are Israelites who want us to stop traveling to Haiti, Africa and Europe and stand here and argue with them about multiple wives because they want to get their freak on. Go do you. As for us, we are going to continue the work of God.

“Yet they sent unto me four times after this sort; and I answered them after the same manner.” They kept bugging Nehemiah to stop the work and argue with them, and he answered the same way again and again, and the fifth time they came with an open letter.

“Thou and the Jews think to rebel: for which cause thou buildest the wall, that thou mayest be their king.” They wrote a make-believe letter accusing Nehemiah of planning to rebel against the king of Persia, and of appointing prophets to preach that there was a king in Judah. Come talk to us, so we don’t have to send this letter to the king.

We are going through this today. Edomites and other nations say we are gathering blacks and Latinos to overthrow the country. That is what France said, when there were about sixty of us. How are you going to overthrow a country like that? Anytime you look out for the welfare of blacks and Latinos it is called racist and hatred and plotting to overthrow the government.

“There are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.” You made all that up.

“For they all made us afraid, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from the work, that it be not done. Now therefore, O God, strengthen my hands.” Nehemiah understood propaganda. This propaganda was to put fear in them and make them stop doing the work, and Nehemiah asked the Lord to strengthen his hands.

Shemaiah said, let us meet in the house of God and shut the doors of the temple, “for they will come to slay thee.” “Should such a man as I flee?” “I will not go in.” “And, lo, I perceived that God had not sent him”: he perceived the trap, this man was trying to set him up, “for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.”

“Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid, and do so, and sin.” It is a sin to stop the work of God out of fear. We can’t let fear overtake us and say, I’m not going to teach any more, I’m not going to do the work of God. That is a sin.

“My God, think thou upon Tobiah and Sanballat according to these their works”: he prays to God to deal with these evil people, “and on the prophetess Noadiah”, a black woman who joined with them, “and the rest of the prophets”, the false prophets who tried to put him in fear and make him stop rebuilding Jerusalem.

The wall was finished in fifty and two days, “and all the heathen that were about us saw these things, they were much cast down in their own eyes: for they perceived that this work was wrought of our God.” That is how they feel when they see black people organized and working together, blacks and Latinos. They know we are the people of God, the people of the book, and they don’t like it. All the people on TikTok, YouTube and Instagram making videos against us to stop this work are doing the same thing that was done back then.

“Moreover in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters unto Tobiah”: the nobles are the bourgeoisie, sending letters to Tobiah, the enemy of our race. “For there were many in Judah sworn unto him”: many Judahites were sworn to this heathen who hated those black Jews.

“Also they reported his good deeds before me”: these nobles, this black bourgeoisie, would go to Nehemiah and tell him how good Tobiah and the enemies of God were: these are good folks, good white folks, good Arab folks. “And uttered my words to him”: whatever Nehemiah said, they reported back. “And Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear.”

The liberal in Trick Baby said it plainly: if we leave a smart one in the ghetto he might develop into a leader against us, but if we raise him up into white society, we neutralize him; he tries to act like us, loses his identity and his racial anger, and becomes alien to his brothers. Racial anger comes from all the injustice done against black people: Trayvon Martin, Tamir Rice, Sandra Bland, Sonya Massey, Kendrick Johnson, Rasheem Carter. When they give black people money and position, the racial anger is gone; hence your entertainers and ball players. Well, guess what’s coming out of the ghetto: 144,000 leaders. And now men like Nick Fuentes say they are done with the token blacks and the DEI hires; they used them because of white guilt and don’t need them any more.

When white society pulls you up and you become that bourgeoisie, the rich famous entertainer or actor, there is an alignment you must have with white supremacy. Even in the Christian church you are forbidden to speak against it. So the black bourgeoisie, let’s say inadvertently, supports oppressive systems. It isn’t the first time; it happened in Egypt.

“The officers of the children of Israel, which Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them”: Pharaoh’s taskmasters set officers from the children of Israel as slave masters over them. There were certain officers of the children of Israel who worked for Pharaoh: black people oppressing black people. Why? Because they made a covenant with Pharaoh for a better living, to be financially well off. These are the ones who wanted to go back to Egypt and remembered the melons, the leeks and the onions, because they were eating good. It is the same thing going on today.
“Ye scornful men, that rule this people which is in Jerusalem”: the rulers of our people, the same nobles we read about.

“We have made a covenant with death”: an agreement with death, and that is the white man today. “And with hell are we at agreement”: the hell they agree with is the low condition of the masses of our people. The bourgeoisie don’t identify with the masses of their own people; they try to live in white society and separate themselves from black and brown people. The Congressional Black Caucus are the Herodians today, paid no less than a million dollars with free health care for life, and they don’t give a damn about you or me.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through”, when judgment comes, “it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge.” They have made Christianity their refuge; that is the lies. They really believe a white man is going to come from the sky and save them. If you see a white man come out of the sky, you’d better run. “And under falsehood have we hid ourselves”: they hid themselves under Christian lies.
“Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone”: that stone is Jesus the Christ, the black Messiah, “a tried stone, a precious corner stone”: he is the leader, “a sure foundation.”
“The hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies”: the judgment that comes is going to sweep away the refuge of Christian lies, “and the waters shall overflow the hiding place.”

“And your covenant with death shall be disannulled”, your agreement with death, the white man, “and your agreement with hell”, with us being in a hellish condition, “shall not stand.” “Then ye shall be trodden down by it”: when judgment comes, they are going to be put to death.

“From the time that it goeth forth it shall take you”: from the time the word goes forth, the understanding shall take hold of you, morning by morning, “by day and by night: and it shall be a vexation only to understand the report.” It is going to vex them just to understand the report of the scriptures. They hear what the prophets say and know they made a covenant with white Christianity and white supremacy and will be judged for it, but the money is good, and they can’t give it up, though they know what is said is right.

“For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it”: that bed is their bed of Christian lies. You can’t get comfortable in it, because you know the lies you learned about John 3:16 aren’t right. “And the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it”: you try to cover yourself in Christian lies like a little blanket and wrap yourself in the comfort of lies, and it is not going to work.

precepts.why:
This shows what they cover themselves with. “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord”: our people are rebellious children, “that take counsel, but not of me”: they take counsel, but not from the Bible, “and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit.”

That goes back to the covering in Isaiah 28:20 that is too narrow to wrap yourself in. You are not covering yourself with the spirit of God; you are covering yourself with lying white supremacy Christianity and the hope that a white man is going to save you, and you know it is all lies. “That they may add sin to sin”: and that is what is going on.

sense.text: “Thus saith the Lord my God; Feed the flock of the slaughter.” Our job is to feed the flock of the slaughter, and we are the slaughtered people. That is what slavery was all about, what Jim Crow and the Black Codes were all about, what the KKK and the Aryan race are about: our slaughter.

“Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich.” Those who sold us into slavery say, bless the Lord, I am rich: the white man made big money selling negroes and Latinos.

“And their own shepherds pity them not”: the Black Caucus and the churches. They are multi-millionaires and don’t give a damn what we go through.

Sékou Touré said it: when you are praised by the colonist, it means you are bad for your people; when they say you are bad, it means you are good for your people; the day they say I’m good, it means I betrayed you. Any black or brown person that white society uplifts is bad for the people. Now the FBI director Kash Patel, an East Indian token, tells the public not to mourn Assata Shakur. You don’t tell us who our heroes are. She worked with the Black Panthers feeding black children, and we are glad the Most High gave her a peaceful passing outside their hands.

“For though thy people Israel be as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of them shall return.” That is happening right now: we number as the sand of the sea, yet a remnant of us is returning. “The consumption decreed shall overflow with righteousness”: righteousness shall flow and flow.

precepts.why: “Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she which travaileth hath brought forth”: the Lord gave us up because we broke his laws. “Then the remnant of his brethren”, Christ’s brethren, that is us, “shall return unto the children of Israel.” Why do we have to return? Because we lost our way and lost our identity. That is the prophecy of the remnant returning.

“Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you.” We were commanded by the Son of God to go into all nations and teach our people in all nations, because we went into slavery and were scattered. That is how the remnant returns.

sense.text: This is the historical context of the prophetic reviving of our people. “Now for a long season Israel hath been without the true God”: as it was back then, so it is today; for a long time we have been without the true God. White Jesus is not the true God. He is an impostor, the Antichrist, the devil. “And without a teaching priest, and without law”: without God’s law.
“But when they in their trouble did turn unto the Lord God of Israel, and sought him, he was found of them.” As it was back then, so it is today: we are turning to the Lord our God.

precepts.why:
Watch what happened: “he sent to his princes”, “to teach in the cities of Judah.” “And with them he sent Levites”, and priests. “And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

What we do is not new. Teachers were always sent out to teach in the streets, in the cities of Judah, with the book of the law, the Bible, in their hands. You thought Christ started that first? It goes way back to Chronicles: go out in the streets and teach. That is the answer to being without a teaching priest.

Jehoshaphat “went out again through the people from Beer–sheba to mount Ephraim, and brought them back unto the Lord God of their fathers.” That is the turning back of 2 Chronicles 15:4. “And he set judges in the land throughout all the fenced cities of Judah, city by city”: order and structure.

“Take heed what ye do: for ye judge not for man, but for the Lord, who is with you in the judgment.” Brothers, when we judge we are not judging for man; we are judging for the Lord. We cannot be partial. To hell with your friend; God doesn’t deal with that friendship stuff.

“For there is no iniquity with the Lord our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts.” Respect of persons is that friendship. A gift is meant to destroy your way of seeing and speaking. That’s why Esau always wants to give you money: so you won’t speak right and won’t see right.

sense.text: There is a need for leaders who acknowledge and address injustice. “The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.” Only the word of God gives understanding to stupid people. All of us at one time were stupid people: we didn’t know our identity or our history. Even if you were at an HBCU, you were following the white man’s customs, so you still fall into the category of the simple.
“I opened my mouth, and panted: for I longed for thy commandments.” We have to long for God’s commandments.

“Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.” Don’t let pornography dominate your life. Don’t let weed dominate your life. Don’t let homosexuality dominate your life. Don’t let crack dominate your life.
“Deliver me from the oppression of man: so will I keep thy precepts.”

In hitting the streets and teaching, what we are doing is making a movement toward repentance and change, reform and transformation.

“For the children of Israel shall abide many days”, centuries, “without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image”: we had no image. Our image was garbage. A Christian on YouTube said teaching black and brown children to love their skin color is racial idolatry, but teaching them the white man was God was fine, and nobody saw anything wrong with that. “And without an ephod”: that is the twelve tribes.

“Afterward”: after those centuries of not knowing, “shall the children of Israel return”, return as Israelites, and that is where we are living right now, “and seek the Lord their God”: we are seeking the Lord our God. “And David their king”: among us is David. Christians can’t explain what David their king means in the last days. “In the latter days” King David is going to be here. We just don’t know who he is. He might be one of your kids.

precepts.why:
“If ye transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations.” That was always the stipulation: if we transgress, God will scatter us among the nations.

“But if ye turn unto me, and keep my commandments, and do them; though there were of you cast out unto the uttermost part of the heaven, yet will I gather them from thence.” No matter how far our people are scattered, he is going to gather the Israelites, “and will bring them unto the place that I have chosen to set my name there”: back to Jerusalem, the place he chose. That is the return of Hosea 3:5.

sense.text: “And how shall they hear without a preacher?” A preacher means a prophet, because to preach means to foretell, and that is what a prophet does. So you brothers are very important in your learning, and you sisters are very important in teaching the children.

“And how shall they preach, except they be sent?” That is what we endeavor to do: send you brothers. But we cannot send brothers who are out of order, not in the spirit, covetous, envious, filled with hatred or lustful. When you go out of the country, women throw themselves at you, so if you have a lust problem you are not the one to send. “How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!”

Some notable men in the Bible were part of the Boulé and the bourgeoisie of their day. “And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians”: Moses was well educated in Egypt. He had to learn about over 300 gods; that is the Boulé teaching, the elite understanding, giving homage to Egyptian gods.

“And was mighty in words and in deeds.” Tell the Christians: Moses did not stutter. He was mighty in words. When Exodus says he did not speak well, it is because he did not speak Hebrew that well, having been raised speaking the Egyptian tongue.

precepts.why:
With all that learning, there is something Moses did that our people in the Boulé and the bourgeoisie can do if they follow him. “By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter”: he gave up being an Egyptian prince.

“Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God.” The bourgeoisie separate themselves from the masses of the people, and Moses was like that in the beginning, but he said, no, I’m going to join my people. They have the option and the ability to do the same.

“Than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.” Moses understood that his fame, his fortune and all the women he had were only for a season, short-lived. When that is gone, then what? Our people in the bourgeoisie make all this money, but what happens when the money runs out, or when destruction comes? That money can’t save you.

sense.text: Here is another. The king spake unto Ashpenaz, the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring “certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes; Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science.” Daniel was very well educated as one of the princes of Israel, and in Babylon he was able to learn “the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans.”
“So nourishing them three years, that at the end thereof they might stand before the king.” He had to do three years of learning before he could stand before the king.

“Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah” were their Hebrew names. The prince of the eunuchs gave them the Gentile, pagan names, Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, like the names some of you still carry today.

We always refer to them by their pagan names, because when Esau teaches this he calls them Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego, not Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. We have to train our minds. They have a custom of it: they refused to call Assata Shakur by her name and called her Joanne Chesimard to show disrespect for her changing it. They did the same with Malcolm and with Muhammad Ali, and they do the same with us.

“But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.” Daniel made a request. You say, I can’t get the sabbath off from my job; did you ask? I can’t wear my beard, I can’t wear a skirt on my job: request it. They allowed Daniel; they may do the same for you. The worst they can say is no.
“Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs.”

precepts.why:
The princes, governors and captains “saw these men, upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed”, because they didn’t bow to the idol. Nebuchadnezzar said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego”, whose servants “yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God.” You’d better have that same mentality.

He made a decree against anyone who spoke amiss against their God, “because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort.” “Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed–nego, in the province of Babylon”: they were promoted, and later they were set as presidents over the country. Keeping God’s law in Babylon, as Daniel purposed in his heart, did not cost them; God lifted them up.

sense.text: “Art not thou that Egyptian”: the chief captain thought Paul was an Egyptian. The Egyptians are like the Dinka tribe: very tall, thin, lanky, dark skinned. It is telling you what Paul looked like.
“I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus, a city in Cilicia”: Cilicia is Turkey. “A citizen of no mean city”: a citizen of no ghetto. Paul was not raised or born in a ghetto.

precepts.why: “I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, and taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers.” Paul came from a very well-educated and financially well-off family. He was born in Turkey and they took him to Jerusalem to learn under Gamaliel. His family had money and they were very well educated. That is how Paul was able to speak all those languages. He had the education and the finances, all under Rome.

With all the education and the wealth Paul had from his family, watch what he says: “I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things.” Paul gave everything up. “And do count them but dung”: dung means doo-doo; he counted them as nothing, “that I may win Christ.”

Although Paul had the education and the wealth, he gave it up to learn and understand Christ. That is the same thing Moses did. Our people in the bourgeoisie can do the same. Nobody is saying go around broke and homeless; take your money, but leave those fraternities and that whole circle and help build in this truth.

sense.text: “Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.” They don’t talk much about his education, but to be a ruler he had position, a seat, like the bourgeois.

“Rabbi, we know that thou art a teacher come from God.” We know: all the Pharisees and Herod knew who Christ was, but because of the hatred and evil in their hearts, their love for darkness and their love for Herod, they would not accept him.
“Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God”: unless you are born again, you cannot see the coming kingdom.

“Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit”: the water goes to the word and the spirit goes to the word. All it means is the word of God. Christians interpret it as being dumped in a river. What does being dumped in a river have to do with anything? You just come out a wet crackhead, whatever you were, you’re just wet.

“Ye must be born again”: all of us, just as he told Nicodemus, must be born again.

“The wind bloweth where it listeth”: when the word of God travels, it goes where it wants. “And thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.” Like this word we are teaching now: we don’t know who online it is touching, who decides to change their life. At camp the person right in front of you might not be the one who repents; it might be the brother or sister way in the back listening who says, I’m going to change my life.
“Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things?” You are a master in Israel and confused about being born again, which means your whole life has to change and start all over.

precepts.why: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word.” That explains the water of John 3:5: the water is the word.

“It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.” That explains the spirit. The words of Christ are spirit and life. So being born of water and of the Spirit means being born of the word of God.

sense.text:
“Joseph of Arimathea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews.” Joseph of Arimathea, another of the bourgeoisie, was a secret disciple of Christ. He didn’t want to lose his wealth or his position, so he followed Christ secretly.

But he “besought Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus”: right then he had to make it known that he was a follower. I want to bury Christ, in my own tomb.
Zaccheus was another bourgeois, a wealthy individual. “The chief among the publicans, and he was rich.” The publicans were the tax collectors for Rome.
“Because he was little of stature”: he might have been five foot, five foot two. He was short.
“A man that is a sinner”: why was Zaccheus called a sinner? Because he was a tax collector doing Rome’s bidding, collecting your taxes, and Israel hated the publicans.

“Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor.” Listen to what he is saying; the word poor will be touched on in Matthew 19. “And if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.”

“This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham. For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.” Zaccheus, this rich man, was lost, but by repenting there is salvation for him. That is the message to our people who are rich and our people who come from these fraternities. It is the same message for them.
“If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” That is the door to salvation.

“Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.” The Christians call this legalism and say you are not supposed to teach the commandments. But Christ taught legalism. He taught God’s laws.

“If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor.” That is the same thing Zaccheus said. But what does it mean by the poor? The mindset of Christianity is to go out in the street and give any random person your money; Philip Anthony Mitchell found a random cracker, a random Edomite, and gave him $50,000, and you never see him give black people that. You never read of Christ or the apostles walking around throwing money at random poor people. The money Christ gave was to Peter, from the first fish, to pay the taxes for them both.

precepts.why: “Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.” This begins to define who the poor are that Christ told the rich man to give to: the poor in spirit, not random people on the street.

“They spake the word of God with boldness. And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul”, and “they had all things common.” “Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold”, and they did not go out into the street and hand it to everybody: they “laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.”

These were men and women who put work in the body. The diligent men and women in the body were the ones helped. That is giving to the poor.

The Christian church taught otherwise. A mother brought a strange homeless man into the house because the pastor said help the poor, and it caused a big fight when the father came home and asked what if this man kills us in the middle of the night. Peter Tosh died because he let a homeless man stay in his house; when he asked for his space back, the man came back with others and shot everyone in the house. Christianity will make you stupid. They did not walk around Jerusalem giving money to homeless people; the money collected was for the men and women of the body, the poor in spirit.

“It is not meet to despise the poor man that hath understanding”: it is not good to hate the poor man that has understanding. “Neither is it convenient to magnify a sinful man.” Giving all your money to a homeless man on the street who is a Muslim, a rapist, or a schizophrenic who stabs you on a train is simple as hell. The poor to be helped are the poor who have understanding.

“Help thy neighbour according to thy power, and beware that thou thyself fall not into the same.” You are not supposed to fall into the same situation he was in.

Years ago a brother had four dollars in his pocket, and another brother asked to borrow four dollars for chicken wings and the train. He gave him all of it, and then came asking everyone else for money because he was broke. Help him according to your power, not so that you become the one in need.

sense.text: “That we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.” The church has you thinking he went to the Chinese and Japanese. That is why precept must be upon precept: the heathen are Israel, the northern kingdom, and the circumcision is the southern kingdom.

“Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.” Does that mean he went around Jerusalem or Asia Minor giving money randomly to people who had no money? No. The poor are the saints, the believers.

precepts.why:
This defines the word heathen. God will not be inquired of by the house of Israel, “And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all, that ye say, We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.” Israel wanted to be like the heathen, and God said no, I will end all that.

So now we know who the heathen are in Galatians 2:9: the Israelites who became as the heathen, the northern kingdom.
“Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.” Paul’s alms were for his nation.

This shows whom Paul was helping. “But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints. For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution”: that is money, “for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.”

“For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.” We give the Gentile Israelites spiritual understanding, and they are to give us carnal things: money. That is the contribution he was talking about, and that is remembering the poor.

“The grace of God bestowed on the churches of Macedonia; How that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.” The riches of their liberality means they gave freely, and it was to the saints in the church.

“For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.” Achaia was ready a year ago and their zeal provoked very many, and Paul sent the brethren before to “make up beforehand your bounty”: your bounty is your money, “that the same might be ready, as a matter of bounty, and not as of covetousness.”

The money he was collecting had nothing to do with covetousness. That is why verse 1 says “as touching the ministering to the saints”: these were men and women of the body who had need.

“Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.” The collection was for the saints, the believers, not random people on the street, which is what the church will have you believe.

sense.text: Back to the Boulé. “But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare”, a trap, “and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” Ask Diddy. Ask R. Kelly.

“For the love of money is the root of all evil.” Tell the Boulé and the bourgeoisie that, because they love money. “Which while some coveted after”: that’s the problem, they coveted after it, “they have erred from the faith”, from the faith of Christ, “and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”
“But thou, O man of God, flee these things; and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, meekness. Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life.”

“Charge them that are rich in this world”: we are to charge the rich, “that they be not highminded.” The high-minded separated themselves from the masses of the people and thought they were better. “Nor trust in uncertain riches”: ask Andrew Tate, whose money they seized. “But in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.”

“That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute”: that goes back to Acts 4, “willing to communicate; Laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come.”

“For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the gospel.” Some thought the mission was to dip people in water. Paul said Christ did not send him to dip people in water; preaching the gospel is the true baptism, not the water.

“Not with wisdom of words”: he is using words to preach, so this means man’s words, the wisdom of this world, philosophy, the BS out there.

“For the preaching of the cross is to them that perish foolishness.” To some of our people who are wealthy and in these fraternities, a black Jesus dying on the cross for anybody is foolishness that won’t do anything for our people. “But unto us which are saved it is the power of God”: preaching that Christ died on the cross for our iniquities is the power of God.

“I will destroy the wisdom of the wise”: you go to all your universities and fraternities, and God says he will destroy all of it, “and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent.” That is why none of them can come against us; none of the Boulé with all their education can come against this truth, so they stand at a distance and listen.

“Where is the disputer of this world?” Everybody wants to dispute for America. What did America do to help you? They let you build schools? You didn’t build those schools; the white man built them.

“The world by wisdom knew not God”: with all the wisdom of the world, they never learned the one true God. “It pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.” People say we waste our time preaching, but that is the power God is using to save many people alive.

“The Greeks seek after wisdom”: the Greeks are the northern kingdom. “But we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness; But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks”: that goes back to 2 Maccabees 4 and 2 Maccabees 6:6. Christ is “the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”
“Because the foolishness of God”, the preaching of the cross, “is wiser than men; and the weakness of God is stronger than men.”

“For ye see your calling, brethren”: brothers, you must see your calling into this truth. Some see it and some don’t. Someone emailed saying he is tired of keeping the commandments and just wants to go back into the world and sin. Bye.

“Not many wise men after the flesh”: Booker T. Washington, James Baldwin, Thurgood Marshall, Marcus Garvey, W. E. B. Du Bois, Frederick Douglass, Malcolm X. “Not many mighty”: Floyd Mayweather, Usain Bolt, Muhammad Ali, Michael Jordan, Tyson, Pelé, LeBron, Tiger Woods, the athletes. “Not many noble”: Obama, Mandela, Colin Powell, Kofi Annan, Tutu. God didn’t choose any of them. He chose you and me.

“But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise”: we are the foolish things, the down and out, the poor. They say we are bums without their education or money, but we have the power of God in our hands. The wise went through all their schools and never came to the understanding we have; they ask, where did you learn that? “And God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty”: we are the weak things, and no athlete can stand against this truth.

“And base things of the world”: we are the base. Paul came from no mean city; we come from mean cities. “And things which are despised”: we are the ones despised. “Yea, and things which are not”: they say we are not even a race, not a people. “To bring to nought things that are”: like their holidays, which we are bringing to nought.

“That no flesh should glory in his presence.” We can’t glory, because there is nothing we did to make God choose us; it is his blessing and favor on us. “Who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption.” “He that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.”
